clue.text: Officer swallows male anger, rising at 9

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one piece goes within another
in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top, so letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A commanding officer bottles up his fury, which boils over at nine o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At 9' looks like a time; 9 is the theme entry VALEDICTION, and many entries here are ways of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a casual British farewell, one of many parting words collected under the theme valediction.

clue.text: Bend and turn over in the manner of 9

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows it

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing
as in a U-bend in a pipe

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so the following word runs backwards

explanation.surface: Instructions for a farewell gesture: bow low and roll over.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is spelt by splitting AIR around the other pieces, so the join falls mid-word rather than at the space.
explanation.definitionFit: Au revoir is the French parting phrase, literally until we see each other again, another theme word for valediction.

clue.text: Put fresh shine on the riposte

explanation.surface: Polishing up a clever comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a curt refusal or snub, the kind of sharp return a riposte delivers.

clue.text: Publication receives one by return — there could be dosh in it

definitions.text: there could be dosh in it

indicators.note: a receiver takes things into itself, so the following words go inside the first piece
by return means coming back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned to YB

explanation.surface: A magazine takes a single contribution in the post, perhaps with cash enclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: MAG takes in ONE plus YB. Dosh is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-bag is a sack or pouch for holding cash, so cash could well be inside one.

clue.text: Insecure at introducing top of designer range

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so the following pieces are placed inside the first word
the top of a word written downwards is its opening letter

parts.note: the Rif is a mountain range in Morocco

explanation.surface: Feeling unsure at the launch of a fashion designer's latest collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adrift is loose and unmoored, so not securely fixed in place.

clue.text: Compound ceremonies after missing the French play

indicators.note: when something is missing it has been left out, so those letters are dropped from the word

explanation.surface: A drama about rituals, minus its French element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' fixes the order: the ceremonies come after the shortened play.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrites is a mineral compound of iron and sulphur, known as fool's gold.

clue.text: Story-teller daily keeping old money back

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning woman

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: the ecu was an old French coin and a former European unit of account

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist holding back some old cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; in British usage a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales, a sequence of stories told by pilgrims.

clue.text: 9's mawkishness, black in colour

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece within the word that follows

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A sentimental farewell, gloomily dressed in black.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye is the everyday parting word, the plainest example of the theme valediction.

clue.text: Last word in lowland accent

explanation.surface: A final remark spoken in a country accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a farewell speech or parting phrase, the closing thing said before leaving.

clue.text: Some rude letters about a stinker

indicators.note: about in the sense of turned around, so the found letters run backwards
some means only part of the following words, so the answer lies within them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Offensive letters written about someone nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The teledu is the Javan stink badger, an animal that sprays a foul smell in defence.

clue.text: Mimicker acquires oomph, if given stimulant

explanation.surface: An impersonator becomes livelier when handed a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before dinner to whet the appetite, so it stirs hunger.

clue.text: 9 — 0 to intelligence

parts.note: a zero read as the letter

explanation.surface: Looks like a football score: nine goals to nil against the spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' means added on to, so the zero is attached after intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is the Italian informal parting word, widely borrowed into English as another theme farewell.

clue.text: Bee and ant flit about, annoyed by one of their ilk

definitions.text: annoyed by one of their ilk

indicators.note: insects flitting about move every which way, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: all ten letters, including those of and

explanation.surface: Insects buzz around and get bitten by a fellow insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Flea-bitten means bitten by fleas, which are insects like the bee and ant, hence one of their kind.

clue.text: Suddenly ceasing to nag biker cryptically?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, a reverse clue: the answer's first word rearranged, with off as a crossword signal, makes nag biker

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a clue itself, the answer says break up the letters of the first word, and they give nag biker.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking off a conversation or relationship means ending it abruptly, without warning.

clue.text: Learned Mozart's sixth "Composition with Horn"

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh
sixth points to the letter in position six of the named word

parts.note: the letter in sixth place of Mozart

explanation.surface: A scholarly study of Mozart's work for horn, like his horn concertos.
explanation.definitionFit: An antlered animal, such as a stag, carries branched horns on its head.

clue.text: 9's vessel capsized in autumn

indicators.note: in places the vessel inside the season word
a capsized boat is upside down, and in a down entry that turns the word backwards

parts.note: a ewer is a water jug

explanation.surface: A ship overturned in the autumn gales, a sad parting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'capsized' suggest a boat; the vessel is a jug. Fall is the American word for autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell is a formal or poignant parting word, another variety of the theme valediction.

clue.text: Guitarist discovered second self the Latin way

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
via is Latin for road or way

explanation.surface: A musician finds a second identity by travelling the Roman road.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrés Segovia was the celebrated Spanish classical guitar virtuoso of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Sweet box containing religion

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a loge is a theatre box

explanation.surface: A box of confectionery with a spiritual message inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a small medicated or flavoured tablet sucked like a boiled candy.

clue.text: Complaint of Queen Mother getting the bird in Hell

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces within the underworld word

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A grievance about the Queen Mother being given the bird, jeered, in hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mother' reads as one royal person but splits into two pieces; 'getting the bird' sounds like being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermatitis is an inflammation of the skin, a medical ailment rather than a grumble.

clue.text: Reckless plan to capture six hundred and one

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner and holding inside, so the following pieces go within the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area

explanation.surface: A rash scheme to seize six hundred and one prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap person or scheme is wildly impulsive, acting without thought for consequences.

clue.text: Wise man takes note of 9

parts.note: Solon was the wise lawgiver of ancient Athens

explanation.surface: A sage jots down a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal parting phrase, one more of the theme's ways of bidding someone goodbye.

clue.text: Mechanical man with no heart for the cause

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and having none means that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A heartless automaton campaigning for a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the central B of ROBOT leaves ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of a problem is its source or origin, the thing that brings it about.

clue.text: Also act about sign of 9

indicators.note: about in the sense of around, so one piece surrounds the other

explanation.surface: Another performance about a gesture of farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty, old-fashioned British way of saying goodbye, fitting the theme valediction.

clue.text: Perhaps advocate putting river god outside

indicators.note: putting signals placing one word in position relative to the other
outside means the god word wraps around the river word

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god
the Wye flows between England and Wales

explanation.surface: Maybe a barrister is pushing a river deity out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is one kind of lawyer, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example of the category.

clue.text: Whence holy calls are introduced to make money

indicators.note: being introduced into something means going inside it

parts.note: to mint is to coin money

explanation.surface: From where sacred appeals are brought in to raise cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the mosque tower from which the muezzin calls Muslims to prayer.

clue.text: A record in unspecified parallel

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces within the word that follows

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A record placed in an unnamed parallel world.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogy is a comparison drawing likeness between two things, a parallel in that sense.
